title: Bell and PhotonFirst sign agreement to advance fiber optic sensing technology for rotorcraft applications
summary: The signing took place during the annual NL-US Defense Industry Days conference.
body_markdown:
Bell Textron Inc. (Bell) and PhotonFirst Technologies B.V. have signed a memorandum of understanding (MoU) to further explore and mature the use of fiber optic sensing technology for advanced structural health monitoring (SHM) applications on Bell aircraft.


The signing took place during the annual NL-US Defense Industry Days conference.


Fiber optic sensing is increasingly being adopted as a next-generation sensing technology for SHM applications. Compared with conventional electrical sensors, optical sensors are inherently immune to electromagnetic interference, can withstand high temperatures and can significantly simplify installation.


Multiple sensing points can be integrated into a single small, lightweight optical fiber, significantly reducing cabling, weight and installation complexity.


These characteristics make this technology particularly suited to monitoring structural integrity of aircraft structures and components throughout their service life.


The collaboration between Bell and PhotonFirst will focus on maturing the technology and further advancing its integration into rotorcraft applications.


The structural data generated can support the transition from scheduled inspections and preventive maintenance toward condition-based and predictive maintenance. This can help Bell’s customers increase fleet availability and reduce maintenance costs.


“Bell is excited to work with PhotonFirst and explore the use of Fiber Optic Sensing technology,” said Jeffrey Schloesser, senior vice president, Strategic Pursuits, Bell Textron Inc.


“By working with PhotonFirst, Bell will find ways to increase sustainability and maintainability in support of our operators’ needs for high mission readiness.”


“For 20 years, we have been developing fiber optic sensing technology for some of the world’s most demanding environments. An aircraft structure is one of those environments, and succeeding there takes more than a good sensor. It requires the right approach to integration, installation and reliability. We’re proud to bring that experience to Bell and work together to turn structural data into better maintenance decisions,” said Leendert-Jan Nijstad, CEO of PhotonFirst.


*This press release was prepared and distributed by PhotonFirst.*
